title: Equality of two selector pair distributions
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $\theta\in[-1,1]$, and let $H:\Omega\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. Draw two independent values from $\pi$ and two signs in $\{\pm1\}$ so that the first sign is uniform and the second equals it with probability $(1+\theta)/2$ and is its negative otherwise; use each sign to select the first or second drawn value, respectively, and apply $H$ to the resulting pair. The expected value equals that obtained by drawing $x$ from $\pi$, then retaining $x$ as the second value with probability $(1+\theta)/2$ and otherwise drawing that second value independently from $\pi$, and applying $H$ to the pair.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
